title: M0 mint payload
description: One intelligence_items mint, authored $0 in-session, in the exact shape the coordinator applies through the guarded write path (mint-item.ts -> sectionBrief -> groundBrief/applyLedgerDiff -> item_gate_a_state), per docs in this directory's MINT-RUNBOOK.md. validate-mint-payload.mjs checks this shape against validate_item_provenance criteria C1-C7 before the coordinator ever touches the DB.
_additionalProperties_note: true (not false) at every level in this schema: authors may attach a `_note`/`_proof_note`/`_domain_note` free-text field anywhere to record how a value was resolved (a source lookup, a deliberate omission) -- see example-payload.json. validate-mint-payload.mjs, the real gate, ignores unknown keys entirely; this schema is a shape reference, not a strict contract.

source_url.description: The live document URL (census_worklist.document_url). Becomes intelligence_items.source_url.

full_brief.description: The authored brief prose (markdown). Criterion 6 requires non-blank; criterion 7 (Gate A) scans this text for figures/deadline-dates. For grade='record' this is NOT synthesized prose -- it is the short extracted description built ONLY by concatenating this payload's own FACT/GAP claims (src/lib/intake/record-facts.mjs's buildRecordFullBrief); still required non-blank (criterion 6 is unconditional on grade).

grade.description: Lane POP (2026-09-01, migration 278). 'brief' (default, omit for the historical behavior) = a synthesized, grounded brief. 'record' = a catalogue record: identity + a short description made ONLY of verbatim FACT/GAP spans, no synthesis, $0. Grade does NOT change which of criteria 1-7 apply -- validate-mint-payload.mjs's grade discriminator adds two ADDITIONAL record-purity kit checks (claim_kind restricted to FACT/GAP; every FACT source_span present in full_brief) on top of the unchanged C1-C7 path. See item-type-required-slots.json's header for why required slots are identical across both grades.

source.description: The resolved registered `sources` row for item.source_url (looked up live by the author before authoring the payload -- see MINT-RUNBOOK.md step 2). Must already exist and be active; this kit mints NOTHING into `sources`.

registry_sources.description: Any OTHER `sources` rows a claim cites (corroborators). Each must be a real, live-registered, active source the author looked up -- never invented.

search_results.description: Mirrors the agent_run_searches rows the mint would write -- one per REAL fetched source. result_content must be the actual fetched text (not a stub) for any URL a FACT claim's span must be found in.

result_content.description: The captured text. Per MINT-RUNBOOK.md's slice-and-rebuild law (Wave MH-3), this must be the FULL fetched document, assembled BY SCRIPT from <=8,000-char slices -- never a hand-copied excerpt. validate-mint-payload.mjs's capture-completeness gate fails any result_content whose length diverges from fetched_length beyond the documented tolerance (batch-001's defect, made structurally impossible).

fetched_length.description: REQUIRED (Wave MH-3). The length, in characters, of the FULL document actually fetched, recorded programmatically at fetch time (e.g. `window.__docs[celex].length`) -- independent of, and never derived from, result_content.length. This is what lets the validator catch a result_content that is silently only an excerpt of what was really fetched (mint-run-001.json defects_found[0]).

archived_source_path.description: Optional (Wave MH-3). Path (relative to the payload file's own directory, or to the validator's --base-dir) to an INDEPENDENTLY produced plain-text archive of this result's full fetched document -- e.g. source-<celex>.txt, written BY SCRIPT from the same slice-and-rebuild pass that produced result_content, never retyped from it. When present, validate-mint-payload.mjs's unicode-integrity check cross-references every FACT source_span citing this result against this file instead of (only) against result_content -- the independent reference mint-run-001.json's defects_found[2] named as the missing piece: a hand-transcription error typed identically into both source_span AND result_content passes an intra-payload comparison no matter how strict, because both fields agree with each other. This file must NOT be produced by copying result_content -- it is the point of independence.

source_span.description: FACT only: the VERBATIM substring copied from source_url's fetched text.

source_url.description: FACT/grounded-ANALYSIS only: which search_results[].result_url (or item.source_url) the span was copied from.

slot_key.description: Required for a claim covering an item_type_required_slots row.
